settingText: Present-day Tyrellis Vault district, an old civic quarter whose museums display unidentified objects from a past everyone assumes is remote.
summary: Theo recognizes an object in a public display as his old attaché satchel before reading the label. The museum calls it an anonymous ritual case from a vanished culture. Adrian tries to leave before Theo can force the chronology question.

dialogueInline.text: The clasp sticks on the left.
How old does the sign say it is?

directionInline.text: No scientific dating. Recognition comes from wear, habit and ownership. The museum label is disturbing because it confidently invented meaning around an object Theo remembers using yesterday in another life.

settingText: Ancient Tyrellis waystation during the war, a quiet kitchen between negotiations rather than a command chamber.
summary: Flux debuts over a cup of something going cold while Afterlight asks why everyone keeps demanding answers from someone who has spent the war learning how many answers can be wrong.

dialogueInline.text: They've been waiting for me since breakfast.

directionInline.text: Introduce Flux as a person before a cosmic strategist: dry, tired, reluctant to become everyone's oracle. No floating equations or probability jargon. Afterlight knows Flux well enough not to be impressed by evasiveness.

settingText: Present-day Tyrellis municipal archive beneath the museum, paper records and reused older bindings.
summary: Rae finds one of her ancient annotations bound into a later civic record. Successive generations of apparent history have treated her handwriting as anonymous source material. The physical chain is too continuous to feel like remote antiquity.

dialogueInline.text: Because nobody preserved it. They just kept using it.

directionInline.text: The clue is mundane reuse. Ancient paper becomes a binding, note, foundation text, household object. Reality did not bury everything beneath geological ages; it built ordinary continuity around things whose meaning was missing.

settingText: Ancient Tyrellis council room, small and tired, with Mero and Flux after others have argued themselves out.
summary: Mero asks Flux which future leaves enough people alive to matter. Flux refuses to convert uncertainty into authorization and tells Mero that every faction now wants prophecy to make responsibility disappear.

dialogueInline.text: You mean which choice lets you sleep.
Then stop asking me to dream for you.
You need to choose without pretending the future chose for you.

directionInline.text: Flux's central ethic is responsibility under uncertainty. Mero is genuinely desperate. Flux refuses because prediction has become a way for leaders to outsource guilt.

settingText: Present-day stairwell beneath Tyrellis archive, old stone continuing seamlessly into modern construction.
summary: Theo asks whether he woke up thousands of years after the war. Adrian finally tells him that the question assumes a clean gap that the Reset did not leave behind.

dialogueInline.text: Then why does everything call us ancient?
Because the world needed a story that connected yesterday to today.

directionInline.text: This is as close as the series should get to explaining apparent history. Adrian describes consequence metaphorically, not mechanism. Do not specify years, suspended aging or chronology physics.

settingText: Ancient Tyrellis balcony overlooking refugee routes at dusk.
summary: Starbreaker asks Flux whether decisive action will prevent the catastrophe he fears. Flux refuses to bless the choice. Starbreaker accuses Flux of hiding behind uncertainty; Flux says certainty has become the most dangerous weapon in the room.

dialogueInline.text: You've seen what happens if I wait.
I've seen what happens if you don't.
Maybe. But I won't turn fear into permission for you.

directionInline.text: Do not make Flux superior or serene. The accusation of cowardice should land because Flux privately fears it may be true. This is a person overwhelmed by possible consequence, not a detached calculation engine.

settingText: Present-day Tyrellis street market above the archive, ordinary evening traffic continuing around ancient foundations.
summary: Theo and Rae step outside and realize the apparent historical story still functions for everyone around them. They debate whether truth restored to them creates any right to disrupt other people's coherent lives.

dialogueInline.text: It's the part you keep skipping.
And if they were there too?
Then we still don't get to decide for them.

directionInline.text: Seed the finale's ethical argument here. Rae's position is not pro-forgetting; it is anti-coercion. Theo's anger at stolen history is valid and growing.

settingText: Ancient Tyrellis kitchen late at night, most lights out, Flux and Afterlight alone again.
summary: Afterlight finds Flux preparing to leave. Flux says everyone now hears only the future they want from them. Afterlight asks where Flux will go; Flux genuinely does not know.

dialogueInline.text: Somewhere nobody asks me what happens next.
Then maybe I'll finally be surprised.

directionInline.text: Give Flux and Afterlight affection. Afterlight should understand that Flux is fraying. Do not signal a magical disappearance yet; let leaving seem like an exhausted personal decision.

settingText: Present-day Tyrellis archive after closing, Adrian finally sitting instead of pacing away from questions.
summary: Adrian admits the Reset did not create a false universe by design. It removed meaning so comprehensively that institutions, stories and ordinary lives settled around the absence. He cannot tell where scar tissue ends and authentic post-Reset history begins.

dialogueInline.text: You don't know where the seam is.
I don't think there is one seam.

directionInline.text: Preserve ambiguity. Replacement history is not a simple fake timeline that can be peeled away. Real lives happened inside the scar. This protects present characters from being reduced to illusions.

settingText: Ancient Tyrellis waystation the morning after Flux said they were leaving.
summary: Mero comes looking for Flux. The cup from the previous night is still on the table. Flux is gone. There is no message that explains where, why, or whether disappearance was voluntary.

dialogueInline.text: When did you last see them?

directionInline.text: Resist spectacle. Flux's disappearance becomes uncanny because nothing marks it. No body, no portal, no residue, no answer. This is a true hole in the historical record, not a Reset artifact.

settingText: Present-day Tyrellis transit platform as Theo and Rae wait for Adrian.
summary: Personal memory fragments return without full context. Theo remembers telling Mero that certainty was becoming contagious. Rae remembers objecting to a word Arbiter used to describe civilians. Both realize their ancient selves were not merely clerks.

dialogueInline.text: I told him everyone was getting addicted to certainty.
About what we called the people inside it.

directionInline.text: Advance from presence to agency without revealing the final choices yet. Their ancient selves had voices, and those voices mattered.

settingText: Present-day Tyrellis transit platform during an otherwise routine departure announcement.
summary: A transit worker with no known connection to Theo or Rae suddenly recognizes an erased district name in the announcement and remembers losing a brother there. The return is no longer confined to the protagonists.

dialogueInline.text: No. That's not what it was called.

directionInline.text: End with ordinary human contradiction, not cosmic spectacle. The worker's grief is real even though present biography says the brother never existed. Adrian understands immediately that the scar is opening beyond the people who intentionally sought memory.
